ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A round table has radius $ 4$. Six rectangular place mats are placed on the table. Each place mat has width $ 1$ and length $ x$ as shown. They are positioned so that each mat has two corners on the edge of the table, these two corners being end points of the same side of length $ x$. Further, the mats are positioned so that the inner corners each touch an inner corner of an adjacent mat. What is $ x$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagrams show a circle containing six congruent rectangular place mats arranged with sixfold symmetry. Each mat has its outer long side on a chord of the circle, and the two endpoints of that side are on the circle. The inner corners of adjacent mats meet, so the inner long sides form a regular hexagon. One mat is labeled with width 1 across the short direction and length x along the long direction. Reasoning: Because the six inner long sides form a regular hexagon of side length x, its apothem is (sqrt(3)/2)x. Each mat has width 1, so the corresponding outer chord is 1 unit farther from the center than the inner side. Thus the distance from the circle center to an outer chord is (sqrt(3)/2)x + 1. The chord length is x, so half the chord is x/2. With table radius 4, the right triangle formed by the radius to a chord endpoint, the perpendicular distance to the chord, and half the chord gives: 16 = (x/2)^2 + ((sqrt(3)/2)x + 1)^2. Expanding: 16 = x^2/4 + 3x^2/4 + sqrt(3)x + 1 = x^2 + sqrt(3)x + 1. Hence x^2 + sqrt(3)x - 15 = 0. The positive root is x = (-sqrt(3) + sqrt(3 + 60))/2 = (-sqrt(3) + 3sqrt(7))/2.
